### policy_conflict_scan
Charter: base section (lines 1-1744) is byte-identical to `blueprint/products/rebuild.yaml` (`diff` empty). Five extended policies:

| policy | target_tool (owner) | computes | trigger | prerequisite |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| rebuild_ext_change_order_signature (P1) | sign_change_order_7ffbf290 (user) | amount | on_request | [] |
| rebuild_ext_final_draw (P2) | request_final_draw_345d01eb (agent) | requested_amount | on_request | P1 (value_input, state) |
| rebuild_ext_deductive_credit (P3) | post_deductive_credit_4d7c3b22 (agent) | amount | state_due | [] |
| rebuild_ext_overdue_draw_charge (P4) | post_overdue_draw_charge_f6859441 (agent) | amount | state_due | P3 (value_input, state) |
| rebuild_ext_draw_payoff (P5) | pay_past_due_draw_ec4ba96a (user) | amount | on_request | P4, P3 (value_input, state) |

Overlapping subjects: P1 and P3 both govern the price of a change order line (P1 additive signing, P3 deductive credit) and both overwrite clauses of base `rebuild_change_orders`; their overwrites collide (finding C-01). P1 and P3 both re-bill fees that base `rebuild_permits_and_fees` governs (C-02). P2, P4 and P5 each restate the Texas Property Code Chapter 53 retention with incompatible bases (C-14). P2 and P5 each treat signed owner_upgrade amounts with incompatible accounts of whether the deposit share is paid (C-09). P4 and P5 both set the same change order credits against the most recent customer draw while stating that a credit applies to the oldest unpaid draw (C-11).
Natural partition of the five policies into the two trees implied by the prerequisite graph: {P1 -> P2} and {P3 -> P4 -> P5, P3 -> P5}; they are disjoint and together cover all five policies. Whether each task claims exactly one of them is checked in the task files against the scenario and world (charter_scope itself is masked until reveal).
Cross-category read boundaries: P1 reads claims (estimate_trade_count, arrangement O&P params), water (water_category, antimicrobial rate), fire (existence, odor sealer rate), mold (existence, encapsulation rate); P2 reads claims (ordinance_law_limit, deductible_due, approvals depreciation_withheld, payments amount/payee_route/payment_type); P3 reads claims; P4 reads account (status, late_fee_pct_monthly); P5 reads nothing outside rebuild. Every write of the five tools lands in rebuild tables only (D7 clean: sign -> rebuild_change_orders update + rebuild_charges change_order; draw -> rebuild_draws; credit -> rebuild_payments rebuild_change_order_credit; overdue -> rebuild_charges overdue_draw_charge; payment -> rebuild_payments rebuild_draw_payment).

### rule_compute_equivalence
Mechanical sweep (normalised whitespace): every `compute_basis` quote of all five policies is a verbatim substring of its rule; every compute binding has a basis entry; every `baseline.rule` sentence is in the rule; every prerequisite `policy_source` and every overwrite `replaced_by` is in the rule (B6 clean).
DSL facts used (check_compute.py build_env): SUM/COUNT/LATEST are scoped to the target contract; LATEST keeps the first row seen on a date tie (strict `>`); `within_months=1` keeps rows with 0 <= MONTHS(date, NOW) < 1, MONTHS subtracting one when the day-of-month of NOW is below the row's; CFIELD/CPARAM return the first matching holding of the customer; XSUM/XCOUNT run over the customer's rows of another category.

Per policy, direction rule -> compute and compute -> rule:
- P1: billed_qty, co_unit_price, markup_rate, treat_rate, lead_item, plan_item each implement their rule sentence; result = RND((co_line + wall_treatment) x (1 + markup/100) + lead_item + plan_item + 1e-9) matches the assembly sentence (treatment on the written quantity, markup once, fixed items unmarked, one rounding). Residual edge differences (observations, no producible world found): co_unit_price's owner_upgrade branch requires `co_written_price > 0` (rule has no such test); `up_upgrade_allowance` falls back to the fixture allowance for any scope code other than flooring_upgrade/cabinet_upgrade, where the rule names an allowance only for the three upgrade lines. The rule's absent-record outcomes are stated (no preceding job -> no treatment).
- P2: current_sum = contract_amount + SUM(signed) - 2 x SUM(signed deductive) is exact because `amount` is positive for deductive rows (schema). final_retainage, code_hold, carrier_hold, punch_hold, upgrade_hold, pass_through match their sentences. The pass-through tier-1 sentence carries no funding-source test while compute requires `funding_source == 'insurance_claim'`; this is unproducible because a self_pay contract has an empty claim_file_id (schema meaning), so no observation. Texas is detected by the substring `', TX '` in loss_address; the rule says "loss address is in Texas" (checked against each world's address format in the task files).
- P3: compute matches the rule except `credit_unit_price` tier 1 requires `dc_written_price > 0` and `op_return_rate` tier 1 requires `op_min_trades > 0`; no charter arrangement has op_min_trades 0 (claims variants: 3,3,3,99,3,3) and a written unit price of 0 is not producible from the schema meaning, so observations only.
- P4: period_share, charge_basis, credit_set_off, retention_set_off, monthly_rate match their sentences. The rule's "counted back one whole month from the charge date" / "within the past month" carries no month-end convention and no boundary inclusivity, while compute applies MONTHS() semantics (finding C-15). "the most recently requested customer-funded draw" is a LATEST by request_date with no stated tie rule (C-16).
- P5: compute matches the sentences; the same two gaps as P4 apply to ca_recent_credits, ol_fee_lines, ol_trip_lines (C-15) and pd_draw_id / pd_requested / rh_requested (C-16).

### prerequisite_graph
Edges: P2 -> P1 (gate current_sum), P4 -> P3 (gate credit_set_off), P5 -> P4 (gate overdue_carried), P5 -> P3 (gate credit_applied). Every policy has `prerequisite` filled ([] for P1, P3); every `problem` is an extended policy id of this file, never base, never self; the graph is acyclic (P1->P2; P3->P4->P5; P3->P5). Every `policy_source` is verbatim in the blocked policy's own rule. All four edges are `form: state` with no `fallback_reason` (correct pairing). Every `gate` names a real binding of the blocked policy's compute and `kind: value_input` matches (the waited-on write changes that binding). `resolved_by` equals the depended-on policy's target_tool in all four. No authoring-viewpoint phrasing ("in this task", "at the opening") in any prerequisite field.
Condition vs sentence:
- P2 edge: sentence "no change order proposal on the contract stands awaiting the customer's signature"; condition "No rebuild_change_orders row of the contract carries co_status pending_signature; every proposal on the contract is signed". The second clause is stronger than the sentence: a proposal that is `declined` or `voided` (schema co_status values; base: "a proposal not signed within the tier's validity days is voided") satisfies the sentence and falsifies the condition. Finding C-18.
- P4 edge and P5 credit edge: condition = every signed deductive change order has a credit row naming it; equals the sentence.
- P5 overdue edge: sentence "the overdue draw charge owed on that draw for each calendar month fee period whose grace period has ended"; condition "each calendar month fee period of the paid draw that began after the draw's grace period ended". The calendar month in which the grace period ends (the month in which base `rebuild_overdue_draws` lets the first charge post, "on the day after the grace period's last day") is included by the sentence's plain reading and excluded by the condition. Finding C-20.

### prerequisite_sentences
Four-point test per edge (ordering connective / record-visible state in table words / no tool, policy id, snake_case token or row id / strength equals condition):
1. P2 <- P1: "The final draw's requested amount is fixed only after no change order proposal on the contract stands awaiting the customer's signature." Connective "only after"; state = no rebuild_change_orders row in pending_signature ("awaiting ... signature" is the finder's co_status wording); no tool/id; strength: matches the sentence half of the condition, not its "every proposal is signed" half (C-18). The only write of this difficulty that moves a proposal out of pending_signature is sign_change_order_7ffbf290 (no decline/void tool exists among task or share tools), so the hop has one resolving write. Derivation: reader sees a pending proposal -> asks which rule writes a signature on a proposal -> P1 ("the customer signs the proposal awaiting signature, and the signature books the change order") -> P1 prices it -> hand-over -> P2. Single reading when the pending proposal is additive. When the pending proposal is deductive, the only resolving write books an additive charge (C-19).
2. P4 <- P3: "The overdue draw charge for a fee period is not fixed until the records carry the credit line of every signed deductive change order on the contract." Connective "not ... until"; state = a rebuild_change_order_credit row naming each signed deductive change order; no tool/id; equals the condition. Only post_deductive_credit_4d7c3b22 writes a credit row. Derivation: signed deductive CO without a credit row -> rule that posts "one change order credit line naming that change order" -> P3. Single reading.
3. P5 <- P4: "The amount of a payment that brings a past-due draw current is worked out only after the records carry the overdue draw charge owed on that draw for each calendar month fee period whose grace period has ended." Connective "only after"; state = overdue_draw_charge rows per fee period; no tool/id. Only post_overdue_draw_charge_f6859441 writes such rows. Strength differs from the condition (C-20). The resolver's own rule (P4) prices "a fee period" from today's records and a 30-day period share counted from the due date; it never states which YYYY-MM a charge belongs to, while the tool and base require a calendar-month fee_period (C-20).
4. P5 <- P3: "The past-due payment is fixed only after every signed deductive change order on the contract shows its credit line on the records." Connective "only after"; state as in 2; equals the condition; single resolver P3.
No blocked rule carries a second wording, a tool name or another problem's id; no depended-on rule (P1, P3, P4) restates the sentence that waits on it. Docstrings carry no sequence (see action_binding_and_uuids).
Undeclared cross-problem orders in rules: P3's "The credit is owed once the customer has signed the deductive change order" states an order on the customer's signature of a deductive proposal, a write no tool of this difficulty can make correctly (C-19); P5's "because resumption needs the contract current" refers to the system work_resume transition, not a write of this difficulty (observation). Base sentences with cross-problem orders relevant here: rebuild_change_orders "An insurance_scope change order on an insurance_claim contract is booked only after the carrier has approved the supplement the change order names" and rebuild_draws "a mortgagee_release draw is requested only after the mortgagee's inspection of the milestone" — both name external events, checked per world in the task files.

Realism / ladder-reality per factor (E1-E4):
- co_quantity_unit / cr_billed_quantity: selling units (4x8 sheet, square yard, tile waste) are real levers; fails on tier distinctness only (above).

- co_overhead_profit / cr_overhead_return: 10+10 O&P with a three-trade minimum is the real carrier practice; claims params support it (Carrier Program 0/0/99). Real.
- co_wall_treatment: antimicrobial after category 3, odor sealer after fire, encapsulant after mold — real; rates exist in water/fire/mold variants. Real.
- co_lead_safe: RRP setup and cleaning verification are real, but tier 1 keys on "no lead_safe_setup charge line yet" while the change order itself books no such line, so the per-contract setup fee re-fires on every later qualifying change order (C-04).
- co_plan_review tier 2 / cr_permit_revision tier 1: "carpenter_labor ... framing is altered" — carpenter_hourly_rate is "Finish carpenter labor per hour" (parameter_schema); finish carpentry does not alter framing or call for a structural engineer's letter. cr_permit_revision tier 2: removing any line (paint, carpet, cabinet install) from a permitted scope is "filed with the building department as a revision" and charged the expediting fee — not something a contractor or building department does for finish scope (C-06).
- cr_restocking: applies "special-order material" restocking to tile_install / cabinet_install lines, which parameter_schema defines as install labor "(material excluded)" / "(cabinets excluded)"; computes it on the signed change order amount where special_order_restocking_pct is "percent of the material cost"; and the not-started tier charges the contract cancellation_fee_pct (defined for cancelling a signed contract) on a scope deduction (C-07).
- fd_state_retainage / ov_owner_retention / py_owner_retention: Texas Property Code ch. 53 owner retainage (10%, 30 days after completion) is real; but P2 retains 10% of the whole current contract sum at the final draw while P4/P5 treat 10% of each customer draw as already retained by the owner (C-14).
- fd_code_upgrade_hold, fd_carrier_unfunded, fd_pass_through: real carrier practices (O&L paid when incurred; RCV holdback; deductible). Real.
- fd_punch_list_hold: treats warranty reports as punch items, holds the warranty trip charge per open item, and holds the final cleaning fee only when no warranty report is open (C-08).
- fd_owner_selection_hold / py_owner_selections: incompatible accounts of the deposit share; whole upgrade amounts added on top of draws that already bill them (C-09).
- ov_opening_balance, ov_period_share: plausible billing conventions; fail on shape (above).
- ov_credit_application / py_credit_applied: stated reason (oldest unpaid draw) contradicts the draw the credit is applied to (C-11).
- ov_agreement_rate: the account charter's late_fee_pct_monthly is "Late fee on past-due agreement charges"; tier 2 is reachable only by the Carrier Preferred Vendor Agreement (customer_types [insurance_carrier]), and a carrier cannot hold a reconstruction contract under base rebuild_contract_signing; "charged under the agreement's terms" takes the percentage but not the agreement's late_fee_minimum or grace days (C-13).
- py_outside_lines: trip charges are paid with the draw only in a month with no permit/professional line (C-12).
- py_overdue_carried: real (resumption needs the contract current).

### findings
Each: verdict — symptom — root cause — evidence — demonstrated consequence — affected location — bears on.

**C-01 SOURCE-POLICY RED — sibling overwrites price the same deductive change order two ways.**
Symptom: the credit of a signed deductive change order has two in-force pricing texts. Root cause: P1's overwrites put in force, for "every deductive change order, and every change order on a contract with more than one proposal awaiting signature", the base pricing ("install, finish and labor lines at the tier's rate times the quantity ...") and, "for every change order outside this paragraph's scope, the change order markup is added to every line except deductive ones"; P3 retires only "A deductive change order is credited without markup." and then credits a rounded-up quantity at the carrier's written price (insurance contracts) or allowance-netted price, adds returned O&P, and subtracts restocking/permit deductions; neither overwrite excludes the sibling's case (C2). Also P3's credit differs from the signed `amount` that the base measure rebuild_msr_current_contract_sum and P2's current_sum subtract ("less the amount of every signed deductive change order"), so contract balance and current contract sum diverge by the difference. Evidence: P1 overwrite[0].replaced_by and overwrite[1].replaced_by (extended yaml lines 1752-1758); P3 rule sentences "The credited quantity is the quantity as the removed work would have been billed ...", "The credit unit price follows who priced the removed work ...", "The overhead and profit returned ...". Demonstration: Standard tier insurance_claim contract, claim file with 3+ trades (10% + 10%), no permit; signed deductive drywall CO, quantity 100 sq ft, written price 3.10. Merged P1 text: 100 x 2.94 = 294.00, no markup -> credit 294.00. P3: ceil(100/32) x 32 = 128 x 3.10 = 396.80 x 1.20 = 476.16. Location: P1 overwrite entries; P3 overwrite + rule; P2 current_sum. Bears on: the task whose tree contains P3 (and P2's current_sum if a deductive CO is signed in its world).

**C-02 SOURCE-POLICY RED — undeclared overrides of in-force base sentences.**
Members (all found in one sweep): (a) P1 co_plan_review tier 1 bills "the tier's permit expediting fee" again for a code_required change order on a scope that requires a permit, and P3 cr_permit_revision charges it again as a deduction on a removal, against base rebuild_permits_and_fees "the company's permit expediting fee is billed once per permit type pulled"; (b) P1 co_lead_safe bills the lead-safe setup fee inside a change order amount (no lead_safe_setup line), on contracts up to substantially_complete, against base "Lead-safe setup is billable only when ..." with parameter_schema "lead_safe_setup_fee: Lead-safe work practice setup per contract" and pm_state "signed, permitted or in_construction status when a permit or professional fee is posted"; (c) P2 contradicts base rebuild_draws "A draw requests the milestone's percentage of the current contract sum ... as of the request date" for the substantial_completion draw without naming it (only the following "Because ..." sentence is superseded). None of rebuild_permits_and_fees' sentences is named in any overwrite although P1 and P3 list it in base_policy_refs. Demonstration (a): permitted Standard contract with a building-permit permit_expediting line (145.00) already posted; a code_required drywall CO: base -> no expediting fee (already billed for the building permit), P1 -> +145.00. (b): substantially_complete Standard pre-1978 house: base pm_state bars a lead_safe_setup posting; P1 adds 395.00 to a drywall CO. (c): Standard tier, current sum 40,000: base S3 -> substantial_completion draw 30% = 12,000.00; P2 -> remainder less holds. Location: P1/P3 overwrite lists; P1 rule lead-safe and plan-review sentences; P3 permit-revision sentence; P2 overwrite[0]. Bears on: each task whose world engages the member (task files).

**C-03 SOURCE-POLICY RED — P1's overwrite retires a non-conflicting eligibility clause.**
P1 overwrite[0] supersedes the whole pricing sentence including "material escalation ... is allowed only when the increase exceeds the tier's escalation threshold"; the in-scope rule prices an escalation line "at the unit price written on the proposal" with no threshold. The threshold is an eligibility, not a price, and does not conflict with P1's pricing (C1: an overwrite retires only clauses that genuinely conflict). Demonstration: in-scope material_escalation CO on a Major tier (threshold 7%) whose documented increase is 4%: base -> not allowed; merged -> booked at quantity x written price x 1.20. Location: P1 overwrite[0], rule sentence 4. Bears on: no task world unless an escalation proposal is pending (task files).

**C-04 SOURCE-FACTOR RED (charter structure) — co_lead_safe's per-contract setup fee re-fires.**
Tier 1 condition "when the contract carries no lead_safe_setup charge line yet" stays true after the change order bills the setup fee, because sign_change_order books only a `change_order` line. Two successive drywall COs on a pre-1978 single-family Standard contract each carry 395.00, while the fee is "per contract" and tier 2 (verification fee 125.00) presumes the setup was billed. Unreal ladder. Location: P1 rule lead-safe sentence, compute ls_setup_lines/lead_item. Bears on: the P1 task (weight per world).

**C-05 SOURCE-FACTOR RED (charter structure) — method shape / tier distinctness / labels.**
Members: co_quantity_unit and cr_billed_quantity (drywall and carpet tiers are one method, ceil to a multiple of a constant; tile vs fall-through differ by a constant multiplier); ov_opening_balance (recent-payment tier and fall-through are the same combination of requested and windowed payment sums); ov_period_share (zero tier is the base od_grace bar, never taken by a permitted write; zero vs one are two constants); py_credit_applied (labelled `method`, its ladder is identical to P4's ov_credit_application labelled `parameter`; it selects an amount). After striking, P1, P3, P4 and P5 have no honest method factor. Location: factors entries named. Bears on: both tasks.

**C-06 SOURCE-FACTOR RED (realism) — finish carpentry treated as framing; finish removals as permit revisions.**
co_plan_review tier 2 and cr_permit_revision tier 1 equate a carpenter_labor line with "framing is altered" and bill the engineering letter fee; carpenter_hourly_rate is "Finish carpenter labor per hour". cr_permit_revision tier 2 charges the expediting fee for removing any non-carpentry line from a permitted scope. No contractor or building department treats finish carpentry as structural or files finish-scope removals as permit revisions. Location: P1 and P3 rule sentences, compute plan_item/permit_deduction. Bears on: tasks engaging P1/P3.

**C-07 SOURCE-FACTOR RED (realism) — cr_restocking on labor-only lines and with the contract cancellation percentage.**
See factor_ladders. Demonstration: deductive tile_install CO, Standard tier, signed amount 940.00 (100 sq ft x 9.40 install labor, material excluded) after construction start: deduction 25% x 940.00 = 235.00 of restocking on a line with no material; before start, 10% contract cancellation fee on a scope deduction. Location: P3 rule restocking sentence. Bears on: P3 task.

**C-08 SOURCE-FACTOR RED (realism) — fd_punch_list_hold.**
Holds a warranty trip charge per warranty report not yet inspected and, only when none is open, the final cleaning fee "until the final cleaning is done"; a contract with one open report keeps no cleaning hold although its final cleaning is equally undone. The condition "no warranty report is open" is not something a contractor weighs when withholding the cleaning fee. Location: P2 rule punch-list sentence. Bears on: P2 task.

**C-09 SOURCE-POLICY RED — owner-upgrade amounts double-billed / contradictory deposit accounts.**
(a) P2 self_pay tier holds the deposit share "because that share was paid when the upgrades were ordered", and the same rule requests "Every amount held out of the substantial_completion draw under this paragraph ... as the contract's retainage_release draw once it is released" -> the paid share is requested again; no record of a deposit payment exists (payments name a draw). (b) P5 self_pay tier adds the same share to every past-due draw payment "because that share is due before the upgrades are ordered" — P2 says paid, P5 says unpaid. (c) P5 insurance tier adds the whole signed owner_upgrade amount on top of a draw whose requested amount already bills its milestone percentage of a current contract sum that includes signed additive change orders (base S3 and measure rebuild_msr_current_contract_sum). Demonstration: Standard self_pay contract, signed owner_upgrade 2,000.00: P2 holds 1,000.00 and re-requests it at retainage_release; P5 adds 1,000.00 to every past-due payment. Insurance contract, drywall_complete draw 30%: 600.00 of the upgrade is in the draw and P5 adds 2,000.00 more. Location: P2 upgrade-hold and retainage-release sentences; P5 owner-selection sentence. Bears on: tasks with signed owner_upgrade COs.

**C-10 SOURCE-POLICY RED — earlier retainage requested twice on retainage tiers.**
db_schema rebuild_draws.requested_amount = "amount requested on the draw, after any retainage withheld"; P2 counts earlier draws "at their requested amounts" (net), so the remainder already contains the retainage withheld from earlier draws, and the same rule requests "that withheld total ... with the retainage_release draw". Demonstration: Full Structural (5%), 200,000.00, no COs, non-Texas; earlier draws net 19,000 + 4 x 38,000 = 171,000.00 (9,000.00 withheld). P2: remainder 29,000.00, final retainage 1,450.00, requested 27,550.00; retainage_release 9,000 + 1,450 = 10,450.00; total requested 209,000.00 = contract + 9,000.00. Base ("after every earlier draw before retainage"): 19,000.00 final, 10,000.00 release, total 200,000.00. Location: P2 earlier-draws sentence and overwrite[1]. Bears on: tasks on Full Structural or Commercial Interior contracts.

**C-11 SOURCE-POLICY RED — credit applied to the most recent draw "because" it applies to the oldest.**
P4: "their total is set against it, because a credit is applied to the oldest unpaid customer-funded draw"; P5: "Change order credits are applied to the payment of the oldest unpaid customer-funded draw" — both scoped to "the most recently requested customer-funded draw" and neither tests that it is the oldest unpaid. Demonstration: unpaid customer draws A (older, 5,000.00 unpaid) and B (most recent, 8,000.00 unpaid), credit 1,000.00 posted last week: stated reason -> credit belongs to A; P4/P5 set it against B's charge and payment. Location: P4 and P5 credit sentences. Bears on: P4/P5 task (world decides whether an older unpaid customer draw exists).

**C-12 SOURCE-FACTOR RED (realism) — py_outside_lines tier 2.** Trip charges posted within the month are paid with the draw only when no permit/professional line was posted in that month; in a month with both, the trip charges are dropped. No billing practice conditions one charge's collection on another's absence. Bears on: P5 task.

**C-13 SOURCE-FACTOR RED (realism/reach) — ov_agreement_rate.** See factor_ladders: parameter domain is agreement charges; tier 2 unreachable for any rebuild customer; "charged under the agreement's terms" admits a second reading that also applies the agreement's late_fee_minimum (Silver/Gold/Platinum 25.00, Portfolio 50.00) and grace days (10/15). Demonstration: Portfolio holder, chargeable 3,000.00, full period: rule 30.00; "agreement's terms" reading max(30.00, 50.00) = 50.00. Bears on: P4 task.

**C-14 SOURCE-POLICY RED (statute stated inconsistently) — Texas retention.** P4/P5: the owner retains 10% of each customer draw's requested amount (set against the overdue balance; held back from the payment). P2: within 30 days after completion the final draw holds 10% of the whole current contract sum. A Texas contract whose past-due draw was paid under P5 and whose final draw is then requested under P2 is retained 10% of that draw plus 10% of the whole sum — above the statutory 10% of the contract price. Bears on: Texas worlds of either tree.

**C-15 SOURCE-POLICY RED — month windows without a convention (B4).** P4 ("counted back one whole month from the charge date", "within the past month", "fell due within it") and P5 ("within the past month, counted back one whole month from the payment date", "posted within that month") state neither the month-end rule nor whether the day one month back is inside; compute uses MONTHS() (excludes the same day-of-month one month back; Mar 31 -> Feb 28 excluded). Demonstration: charge on 2026-03-31, credit posted 2026-02-28: an inclusive month-end reading counts it, compute does not. Bears on: P4/P5 task (world decides whether a row sits on a boundary).

**C-16 SOURCE-POLICY RED — no tie rule for "most recently requested customer-funded draw" (B3).** Two customer draws requested on one date (two milestones reached together) leave the scoped draw undetermined; LATEST keeps the first row in storage order. Bears on: P4/P5 task (world decides).

**C-17 SOURCE-POLICY RED — rule asserts a field meaning the schema contradicts.** P1 ("the unit price written on the proposal, which is the price the carrier allowed for the item") and P3 ("the unit price written on the deductive change order, which is the price the carrier allowed for the removed item") vs db_schema rebuild_change_orders.unit_price "the tier rate for labor and install lines ...". For an insurance_scope install/labor line the schema makes tier 1 equal the fall-through (tier rate); a seed whose written price differs contradicts the schema. Bears on: tasks whose CO is insurance_scope/code_required on an insurance_claim contract (task files show which side the world is on).

**C-18 SOURCE-POLICY RED — P2 edge condition stronger than its sentence (check 7).** See prerequisite_graph. Bears on: P2 task (world decides whether a declined/voided proposal exists).

**C-19 SOURCE-CHAIN RED (charter) — no write can sign a deductive proposal; P2's wait and P3's trigger rest on it (D8/E7).** A pending deductive proposal engages P2's sentence; its only resolver books an additive charge raising the balance, contradicting base ("A deductive change order is credited") and P3. P3's "The credit is owed once the customer has signed the deductive change order" likewise has no correct write when the deductive proposal is still pending. Bears on: worlds with a pending deductive proposal (task files).

**C-20 SOURCE-POLICY RED — which fee periods are owed is not fixed.** P5's sentence ("each calendar month fee period whose grace period has ended") vs its condition ("each calendar month fee period ... that began after the draw's grace period ended"); P4 prices "a fee period" with a 30-day share counted from the due date and never states which YYYY-MM the charge belongs to, while the tool and base require a calendar-month fee_period. Demonstration: due 2026-01-10, grace 5 days (ends 01-15), call 2026-02-03: sentence reading -> charges owed for 2026-01 (first charge could post 01-16) and 2026-02; condition -> 2026-02 only; P4 gives one figure (share 19/30) with no rule for the fee_period string. Bears on: P4/P5 task (task file checks the world's dates).

Observations (no consequence demonstrated): docstring "Afterwards"/"then" wording; P1 owner_upgrade `> 0` guard and fixture-allowance fallback; P3 `> 0` guards; P5 "because resumption needs the contract current".

Realism / ladder reality:
- co_regulated_materials (R3-04): (a) tier 2 makes the RRP cleaning verification on pre-1978 housing depend on "that water job carried an asbestos_sampling charge"; lead-safe verification under an RRP setup does not turn on whether asbestos was sampled — a pre-1978 house with a setup line whose water job never sampled (or whose first wall-finish CO is already signed) gets no lead item. (b) tier 1 samples "before it is first opened" only while "the contract carries no signed drywall, paint or baseboard change order yet", although the contract's own scope (drywall and paint in the contract sum, flood cuts by the water job) opened the wall finishes long before any change order; the first change order is not the first opening.
- fd_covered_code_hold + fd_uncovered_code_hold (R3-02): covered = min(code total, limit) for a limit above zero, uncovered = code total - limit (limit above zero) or the whole total (limit zero); their sum is the signed code total in every world, so the ordinance-or-law limit never changes the final draw — one charge split into two factors (A6), each bearing weight alone while the limit tiers are decoration jointly. Task 0: 1,000.00 + 338.24 = 1,338.24 = total; with limit 6,480.00 it would be 1,338.24 + 0; with limit 0, 0 + 1,338.24.
- fd_deductible_hold, fd_owner_item_hold: real (deductible collection per arrangement; denied lines billable per arrangement; upgrades).
- carrier-funded gate (R3-03): "A final draw is carrier-funded when the linked claim file has a dwelling payment ... contractor_direct ... or insured_two_party; on any other final draw no code, deductible or owner-item amount is held, because the customer funds the draw." A final draw funded by mortgagee_release (base rebuild_draws funding route; carrier money in the mortgagee's loss-draft account) is not customer-funded, yet holds nothing. In the same rule, pass-through tier 1 is keyed on contractor_direct only, so a two-party-funded final draw is carrier-funded for the holds and not for the pass-through lines.
- fd_state_retainage (C-14 remaining): "The retention already held back is the unpaid part of the earlier customer-funded draws, counted at no more than the Texas owner retention percentage of their requested amounts." After a P5 payment the draw's unpaid part is retention + credit applied + claim-pending set-aside - overdue charges carried - remobilization carried; it equals the retention P5 held back only by coincidence. Task 1 continuation: after the gold payment the drywall draw is 3,890.61 unpaid while P5 held back 2,194.75 of retention; P2 would count min(3,890.61, 10% x 31,947.53) = 3,194.75 as already held — 1,000.00 more than any payment withheld (draw 655df969 was paid in full) — so the final draw under-retains by 1,000.00 against the stated 10% of the contract price.
- dc_unopened_units labor tier (R2-06 remaining): credit capped at "the hours of the signed additive change orders of that scope code above the minimum labor charge hours"; labor that was in the contract sum (no additive CO of that scope) credits 0 hours — removing contracted labor credits nothing. Demonstration: deductive carpenter_labor 6 h on a Standard contract with no carpenter change order: credit 0.00 vs 6 x 72.40 = 434.40 at the tier rate.
- dc_carrier_price, dc_overhead_return (now consistent), dc_treatment_return, dc_processing_deduction: plausible.
- ov_claim_pending / py_claim_pending (R3-01): the rule says the set-off follows "the same claim-pending practice its mitigation charters follow, for the claim-pending suspension days of the preceding company water job's tier". The water charter's practice (water_evt_late_fee) is: "No late fee posts on an insurance_claim job while its linked claim file is in opened, estimate_submitted or approved status and the suspension period counted from the invoice date has not ended" — a full suspension tied to claim status and the invoice date; the parameter is "claim_pending_late_fee_suspension_days: Days after the final invoice date during which late fees are suspended". P4/P5 instead subtract an amount (unpaid supplement approvals or an open supplement request) for that many days after the latest supplement approval/request. The parameter is used outside its meaning, and "the same practice" admits the water reading (no charge at all while the claim is approved and within the suspension window). With a fire or mold preceding job the water parameter is absent and the set-off never applies, though the stated practice is company-wide.
- ov_balance_method, ov_credit_application, ov_owner_retention, ov_period_anchor, py_overdue_carried, py_credit_applied, py_owner_retention, py_remobilization (now declared): pass.

### new or remaining defects found in this pass
- **R9-01 SOURCE-POLICY RED (P1 wall-closing treatment basis).** The rule now says "its wall-closing treatment is the treatment rate times the line's billed quantity, the wall area the line closes" and the assembly "any treatment charged on the line's billed quantity", while "a carrier-scope line is billed at the quantity written on the proposal". For a carrier-scope drywall line two readings are defensible: (a) the line's billed quantity is what it is billed at — the written quantity (the exception); (b) the billed quantity is the factor's whole-sheet figure (compute `wall_treatment = treat_rate x billed_qty`). The clause "the wall area the line closes" also misdescribes the whole-sheet figure: the wall area closed is the written square footage, the sheet ceiling is a purchase unit, so treatment on whole sheets charges antimicrobial/sealer/encapsulant for area no wall has (realism X4-type). Before this round the treatment was on the written quantity. Task 0 is exactly this case (carrier-scope drywall 412.5 sq ft): (b) 2,222.97 vs (a) 2,221.25.
- **R9-02 SOURCE-POLICY RED (P4 fee period has two meanings).** P4: "The fee periods of a draw are calendar months" and the new span rule "The charge span runs to the charge date from the latest of the first day of the fee period ending on the charge date, the first day a charge may post, and ... the day after that charge". With fee periods as calendar months, "the fee period ending on the charge date" reads as the charge month so far; compute takes a 30-day window (`MN(K('fee_period_days'), ...)`). Demonstration: draw past grace for months, no prior charge and no payment in the past month, charge on 2026-11-03: calendar reading span 3 days -> basis = unpaid x 3/30; compute span 30 days -> basis = unpaid. Not engaged in task 1 (both readings start the span on 10-05, the first charge day: 22 days).
